info.notes: Students with credit for CHEM 120 or 125 may not take this course for further credit.
info.description: Builds upon the principles of chemistry through a lecture and laboratory experience to develop problem-solving skills with a focus on learning trends in the periodic table, electronic structure of atoms and molecules, chemical bonding, chemical stoichiometry, the energetics of chemical reactions, and properties of gases, liquids, and solids. This course includes a laboratory component.
info.title: General Chemistry and Laboratory I
info.departmentalUgradNotes: A grade of C- or better is required for all prerequisite courses.
info.prerequisites: Chemistry 12 with a minimum grade of B, or CHEM 111 with a minimum grade of C- or CHEM 110 and 115, both with a minimum grade of C-.

info.requirements: Attendance at all laboratory sessions is mandatory. Students who are unable to attend a laboratory session due to illness or other exceptional circumstances should notify their instructor before the scheduled laboratory session whenever possible, or within 24 hours of the missed session, to arrange a makeup laboratory session, subject to instructor approval.
info.gradingNotes: Students must complete all six experiments and earn at least 50% in the laboratory portion to be eligible to receive a prerequisite grade of C- or better. Otherwise, a grade of D, N or F will be assigned.
info.courseDetails:
Please note, this course outline was accurate at the time of publication but it subject to change.

Mode of Teaching
  • 3 lecture hours per week
  • 1 tutorial hour per week
  • 4 laboratory hours on alternate weeks

Lecture Topics:
  • Atoms, Molecules, and Ions
  • Stoichiometry
  • Chemical Reactions
  • Gases
  • Thermochemistry
  • Atomic Theory
  • Chemical Bonding
  • Liquids and Solids
  • Solutions
  • Nuclear Chemistry and Radiochemistry (may not be covered in all course offerings)


Laboratory Topics:

Students will complete six laboratory experiments designed to reinforce lecture concepts. Laboratory activities may include topics such as chemical reactions, stoichiometry, redox chemistry, gas laws, thermochemistry, and intermolecular forces.
info.materials:
Required Materials
  • Non-programmable, non-graphing calculator
  • Lab coat and safety glasses/goggles
